s: Who was the last Ikshvaku ruler?
x:
Rudra Purushadatta is regarded as the last ruler of the Ikshvaku dynasty, which ruled from Vijayapuri (Nagarjunakonda) during the 3rd century CE. The Ikshvakus succeeded the Satavahanas in the Krishna Valley and became great patrons of both Buddhism and Brahmanism. During their rule, Nagarjunakonda developed into one of the most important Buddhist centres in India. After the reign of Rudra Purushadatta, the Ikshvaku kingdom declined, and the Pallavas expanded into the region and occupied Vijayapuri. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).

s: Which Vishnukundin ruler had transferred the capital from Amarapuri to Denduluru?

The Vishnukundins emerged as an important dynasty in the Deccan after the decline of the Ikshvakus and the Salankayanas. Their early capital was Amarapuri (identified with Amaravati region). As the kingdom expanded towards the coastal Andhra region, Madhavavarma II shifted the capital to Denduluru (near present-day Eluru in West Godavari district). This strategic shift enabled better control over the fertile Vengi region and facilitated administration of the eastern coastal territories. Madhavavarma II was the most powerful ruler of the dynasty. He assumed the title Janasraya, performed several Vedic sacrifices such as the Ashvamedha, and greatly expanded the kingdom. Option (3): Govindavarma – Founder of the Vishnukundin dynasty. During his reign, the capital remained at Amarapuri.
Option (4): Manchana Bhattaraka – A later ruler who ruled during the declining phase of the dynasty and did not shift the capital.

The Undavalli Caves, situated near Vijayawada on the banks of the Krishna River, are among the finest examples of rock-cut architecture in Andhra Pradesh. These caves were excavated during the Vishnukundin period (5th–6th Century CE). Although they were originally developed as Buddhist monastic caves, they were later converted into Hindu cave temples. The most striking feature of the caves is the monolithic reclining image of Lord Vishnu (Anantasayana Vishnu) carved from a single block of granite. The caves consist of four storeys, displaying remarkable rock-cut architectural skill and reflecting the transition from Buddhist to Hindu religious traditions. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).
